extracted.intended_audience: clinicians, researchers, and authors preparing/publishing clinical case reports (and journal editors/reviewers interested in reporting standards)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and reporting clinical case reports to maximize completeness, transparency, and usefulness of point-of-care data; includes a downloadable CARE checklist, explanation/elaboration paper, and specialty extensions. Applicable to whole reports of observational case reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of CARE Guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: For completeness, transparency and data analysis in case reports and data from the point of care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The CARE Guidelines are intended to ensure case reports contain the information necessary for transparent reporting and for the data to be useful for analysis; the CARE checklist (PDF) operationalizes this purpose. See the linked explanation and elaboration paper for detailed rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the CARE Checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should use the CARE Checklist when writing case reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The CARE Checklist is available to download as a free PDF and as an online fillable checklist (via GoodReports). The checklist provides the specific items authors should address; users are directed to the checklist file for the concrete itemization of required/reporting elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability to whole report
rubrics_metrics.description: The CARE guideline applies to the whole case report rather than to a single section only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should apply the CARE standards across all sections of the report to achieve completeness and transparency. The EQUATOR entry explicitly notes 'Applies to the whole report.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Study design applicability (observational/case report)
rubrics_metrics.description: CARE is a reporting guideline for observational studies, specifically case reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guideline is targeted at case reports (a form of observational study). Authors should treat CARE as the appropriate reporting standard when preparing clinical case reports for publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the CARE flow diagram for systematic data collection
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow the CARE steering group's flow diagram for collecting data when seeing a patient or doing a chart review so information can be systematically recorded for a case report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A downloadable CARE Flow Diagram (PDF) is provided to help clinicians collect the right data prospectively or during chart review to facilitate writing a CARE-compliant case report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include timelines and use provided timeline guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should incorporate timelines in case reports and may use the provided timeline examples and instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional free-to-access information on timeline examples and instructions for creating timelines is available online (links provided). Timelines are recommended to clarify sequence of events in a case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult the CARE explanation and elaboration document
rubrics_metrics.description: Refer to the CARE explanation & elaboration paper for detailed guidance on each checklist item.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The EQUATOR page links to an explanation and elaboration paper (J Clin Epidemiol. 2017) that expands on the checklist items, giving rationale, examples, and clarifications for authors and reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use specialty extensions or adaptations when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: When reporting case reports in a specialty area, use CARE extensions or adapted versions (e.g., CARE‑radiology, CARE‑acupuncture, therapeutic massage adaptation, PhyCARE, CARE‑DN).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The EQUATOR entry lists several specialty extensions and adaptations with citations; authors in those specialties should adopt the extension relevant to their field to capture domain-specific reporting needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make use of translations and resources in other languages
rubrics_metrics.description: The CARE Checklist and associated materials are available in multiple languages and should be used in the appropriate language when available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The checklist and writing outline have been translated into various languages (links provided), and the CARE guideline paper has at least an Italian translation; resources are available via the CARE website and external resource pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of online tools (GoodReports) to assist reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may use online tools (e.g., GoodReports) that provide fillable CARE checklists to complete reporting requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EQUATOR notes an online fillable CARE checklist on GoodReports to help authors structure their report according to CARE items before submission.
